notes.meaning: Jesus knew what the people of his hometown were thinking. They expected him to prove himself by doing the same miracles they had heard he did in Capernaum. They felt entitled to his help simply because he had grown up among them.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars believe Luke placed this visit to Nazareth early in Jesus' ministry to illustrate his general reception, even though the miracles in Capernaum took place before it.

notes.meaning: Jesus told them that a prophet is rarely accepted or respected by his own neighbors. People who watched him grow up as an ordinary boy struggled to recognize his divine calling. Familiarity blinded them to God's work right in front of them.

Jesus reminded them of the great drought during the days of the prophet Elijah, which lasted three and a half years and caused severe famine. Even though there were many needy widows in Israel, God did not send Elijah to help any of them.

Instead, God sent Elijah outside of Israel to a Gentile widow in the foreign town of Zarephath. God chose to show his mercy and miraculous provision to an outsider rather than to his own covenant people.

Jesus also pointed out that many people in Israel suffered from leprosy, a painful skin disease, during the time of the prophet Elisha. Yet God did not heal any Israelites through Elisha, choosing only to cleanse Naaman, an enemy commander from Syria.

The people in the synagogue became furious when they heard these stories. They understood that Jesus was rebuking their lack of faith and warning that God's blessing would pass them by and go to Gentiles.

The mob leaped up, forced Jesus out of the synagogue, and drove him to the edge of the hill where their town was built. In their uncontrolled anger, they intended to execute him on the spot by throwing him off the cliff.

Jesus walked straight through the middle of the hostile crowd and went on his way unharmed. He was completely safe until his appointed time, because no one could take his life before his work was finished.

differ.view: Jesus was rescued by a miracle of divine power, as God restrained the mob by blinding their eyes, holding their hands, or stunning their minds.
Jesus may have been made invisible or so overawed the crowd by His divine presence that they lost all power to lay hands on Him.
No supernatural miracle was needed, because the calm moral majesty of a holy person can naturally disarm an angry mob.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Jesus performed a clear miracle that showed His divinity by making His attackers powerless to touch Him.

notes.meaning: Jesus traveled down to Capernaum, a town on the Sea of Galilee, and made it his new home base. On the Sabbath, the weekly Jewish day of rest and worship, he went into the synagogue and taught the people.
The people listening to Jesus were astonished by his message. The local scribes usually just quoted human traditions, but Jesus spoke with the direct power and authority of God.
A man possessed by an unclean demon, or evil spirit, was present in the synagogue while Jesus was teaching. Confronted by the holiness and truth of Jesus, the demon shrieked at the top of its voice.
The evil spirit screamed in fear, asking if Jesus had come to destroy all the forces of darkness. It openly declared that Jesus was the Holy One of God, recognizing his absolute purity and authority.
Jesus commanded the evil spirit to be silent and ordered it to leave the man at once. The demon violently threw the man to the ground before the crowd, but Jesus' power kept the man from being hurt.
Everyone in the synagogue was filled with wonder at what had happened. They marveled that Jesus did not need magical charms or long rituals, but drove out evil spirits simply by commanding them.
News about this astonishing miracle quickly spread across the entire surrounding region of Galilee. People everywhere began talking about Jesus and the amazing power he displayed.
After leaving the synagogue, Jesus went to the home of Simon Peter in Capernaum. Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a severe fever, and the family immediately asked Jesus to heal her.

Jesus stood over her and commanded the fever to leave, treating sickness as something under his direct control. The fever left her instantly, and she felt well enough to get up right away and serve her guests.

At sunset, the Sabbath ended, so people were legally allowed to carry the sick through the town. Crowds brought loved ones suffering from all kinds of illnesses, and Jesus laid his hands on every single person and healed them.
Demons came out of many people, shouting that Jesus was the Son of God, the promised Messiah. Jesus silenced them immediately because he refused to let evil spirits testify about who he was.
At daybreak, Jesus left the house and went out to a quiet, solitary place to pray. The crowds searched until they found him, and they pleaded with him not to leave their town.

Jesus told them that he could not stay, because he needed to proclaim the good news of God's kingdom to other towns as well. He reminded them that preaching this message was the very purpose for which God had sent him.
Jesus continued traveling and preaching in synagogues throughout the Jewish towns. He stayed faithful to his mission, making sure that many different communities heard the good news.
